answer: Before static content is offloaded, the host must own upload validation, origin protection and prewarming for a release. It must also own deliberate cache keys and cache lifetimes, an explicit authorization boundary (especially for private assets signed at the edge), and a retained version that is the rollback path; garbage collection may delete old objects only after the rollback window, and a deleted object needs a tombstone or purge proof. Purge caches when needed, but account for propagation time and browser caches. If a second origin or duplicated manifest exists, one version authority must own it, and edge configuration must not be unowned.
